import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Check if any feature shows significant association with outcome
    # using Welch's t-test and logistic regression
    if not feats.ids:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Calculate t-statistics and p-values for all features
    t_stats = []
    p_values = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        col = feats.column(fid)
        x = feats.x[:, col]
        y = feats.y
        
        # Welch's t-test
        group0 = x[y == 0]
        group1 = x[y == 1]
        
        if len(group0) > 1 and len(group1) > 1:
            t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(group0, group1, equal_var=False)
            t_stats.append(t_stat)
            p_values.append(p_val)
        else:
            t_stats.append(0)
            p_values.append(1.0)
    
    # Select features with p < 0.05 and |t| > 2
    significant_features = []
    for i, (fid, p, t) in enumerate(zip(feats.ids, p_values, t_stats)):
        if p < 0.05 and abs(t) > 2:
            significant_features.append((fid, abs(t)))
    
    # Sort by significance
    significant_features.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    
    # If no significant features, return empty design
    if not significant_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Check for near-duplicates (correlation >= 0.6)
    # Build correlation matrix to identify near-duplicates
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    near_duplicates = set()
    
    # Identify pairs with |r| >= 0.6
    for i in range(len(feats.ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(feats.ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i, j]) >= 0.6:
                fid1, fid2 = feats.ids[i], feats.ids[j]
                near_duplicates.add((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Remove near-duplicates (keep first occurrence)
    selected_features = []
    seen = set()
    for fid, _ in significant_features:
        # Check if this feature or its duplicate is already selected
        skip = False
        for dup_pair in near_duplicates:
            if fid in dup_pair:
                other_fid = dup_pair[0] if dup_pair[1] == fid else dup_pair[1]
                if other_fid in seen:
                    skip = True
                    break
        if not skip:
            selected_features.append(fid)
            seen.add(fid)
    
    # Limit to MAX_DRIVERS
    selected_features = selected_features[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    # Check if we have enough features for a meaningful model
    if not selected_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Test whether these features show consistent effects across strata
    strata = list(set(feats.stratum))
    if len(strata) <= 1:
        # No stratification, proceed with top features
        drivers = tuple(selected_features)
    else:
        # Check consistency across strata
        stratum_effects = []
        for s in strata:
            mask = [i for i, label in enumerate(feats.stratum) if label == s]
            if len(mask) < 2:
                continue
                
            x_stratum = feats.x[mask]
            y_stratum = feats.y[mask]
            
            # Compute effect sizes for each feature in this stratum
            effects = []
            for i, fid in enumerate(selected_features):
                col = feats.column(fid)
                x_col = x_stratum[:, col]
                group0 = x_col[y_stratum == 0]
                group1 = x_col[y_stratum == 1]
                
                if len(group0) > 1 and len(group1) > 1:
                    t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(group0, group1, equal_var=False)
                    effects.append(abs(t_stat))
                else:
                    effects.append(0)
            
            stratum_effects.append(effects)
        
        # Check if effect sizes are consistent (not too variable)
        if len(stratum_effects) >= 2:
            # Standard deviation of effect sizes across strata
            effect_means = np.array(stratum_effects).mean(axis=0)
            effect_stds = np.array(stratum_effects).std(axis=0)
            # If std/mean ratio is low, effects are consistent
            # This is a simplified test
            if not np.any(effect_means > 0) or np.all(effect_stds / (effect_means + 1e-8) < 0.5):
                drivers = tuple(selected_features)
            else:
                drivers = ()
        else:
            drivers = tuple(selected_features)
    
    # Return final design
    return Design(
        drivers=drivers,
        columns=tuple(selected_features),
        products=(),
        loadings={fid: 1.0 for fid in selected_features}
    )
